question.text: Three members of the House of Medici went on to hold this office in Rome, taking the names Leo X, Clement VII, and Leo XI.
question.answerHtml: Pope [or “the papacy;” or Supreme Pontiff; or Pontifex Maximus; or Bishop of Rome]
question.clue: This position was subject to increased noble control during the pornocracy, and the last English holder of this position was Nicholas Breakspear.

swap.text: This pope, who served during World War II, has been called "Hitler's Pope" for not doing enough to stop the Holocaust.
swap.clue: While on trial, Karl Wolff testified that he had been ordered to kidnap this leader, who gave a "Christmas Broadcast" in support of one group who had "been consigned to death or to a slow decline".

question.leadin: This term sometimes refers to the period of antipopes during the Avignon Papacy.
question.text: Name this term which also applies to an exile of Jews from Judah begun by Nebuchadnezzar and ended by Cyrus the Great.
question.clue: This period in which Philip IV of France moved the Papacy to Avignon, named after a duration of time in the Old Testament.

swap.leadin: Due to their military-like structure, members of this group are sometimes called "God's Marines."
swap.text: Name this Catholic religious order founded by Ignatius Loyola. Members of this group included Francis Xavier, who traveled to Japan as a missionary.
swap.clue: Two members of this group prepared the translation of the Treaty of Nerchinsk and another created a lunisolar calendar for the last Ming emperor.

question.text: This Pope began the First Crusade by offering a remission of sins to those who joined it and supposedly saying "Deus vult," or "God wills it" at the Council of Clermont.
question.clue: This pope allied himself with Roger I of Sicily, and he was heavily influenced by a delegation sent by Alexius I Komnenos.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about knightly orders.
swap.text: Members of this order initially stationed themselves at Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem. This order was dissolved in the early 14th century by Pope Clement V after accusations of fraud and heresy from King Philip IV of France.
swap.answerHtml: Knights Templar [or Templars; or Templiers; or Poor Fellow-Soldiers of Christ and of the Temple of Solomon; or Pauperes commilitones Christi Templique Salomonici; or Order of the Temple; or Ordre du Temple]
swap.clue: Members of this rival to the Hospitallers were purchased and executed en masse by Saladin after he won the Battle of Hattin.

question.leadin: Terrorists planned to assassinate this pope during a visit to the Philippines in the first phase of the Bojinka Plot.
question.text: Name this pope who established World Youth Day in 1985. This pope's visit to his home country motivated the formation of the Solidarity movement, which went on to end communist rule in that country.
question.clue: This man made a prison visit to forgive Mehmet Ali Agca, a member of the Grey Wolves who tried to kill him.

swap.leadin: This council attempted to mediate between the Teutonic Knights and Jogaila and Vytautas of Poland and Lithuania, respectively.
swap.text: Name this council that elected Pope Martin V, ending the Western Schism and the Avignon Papacy. It also ordered theologian Jan Hus burned at the stake.
swap.clue: Other decisions included the canonization of St. Bridget of Sweden and a voting of special privilege to Emperor Sigismund, who had called this meeting.

question.leadin: Name these other medieval groups of knights.
question.text: This French militant group, formed from the Order of St. John of Jerusalem, was based on Rhodes after capturing the island from the Byzantines. In 1522, they became the Knights of Malta, and they are still in existence under that banner.
question.clue: The island of Gozo was used by Turgut Reis to stage a series of assaults on this group's stronghold, during which Philip II of Spain sent this group significant aid.

swap.text: The victorious confederation at Lepanto, led by Don Juan of Austria, was known by this name due to the participation of the Papal States.
swap.clue: One of the members of a better-known group of this name won an important battle at Guinegate, also known as the Battle of the Spurs, and two year prior it defeated French forces at the battle of Novarra.

question.leadin: Identify the following about a church council.
question.text: Called for the purpose of ending the Great Schism, this 1414 council compelled all three competing popes to withdraw and elected Martin V.

swap.text: A pope by this name excommunicated the Holy Roman Emperor during the Investiture Controversy. Another pope of this name replaced the Julian calendar with a namesake calendar.
swap.clue: Henry IV walked to Canossa in a hair shirt to have an excommunication that was given to him by a pope of this name rescinded during the Investiture Controversy.

question.text: The fifth pope to take this name suppressed the Templars at the Council of Vienne and moved the papacy to Avignon, thus beginning the Babylonian Captivity.
question.clue: He rescinded an earlier papal bull which proclaimed that outside of the church, there is no salvation.

swap.text: One of these splits in the Christian church arose when Gregory XI moved the papacy back to Rome. The split between the Orthodox and Catholic church in 1054 is known as the "Great" one of these.
swap.clue: This breaks and splits in the Christian church. The "Great" one resulted in the formation of the Catholic Church, while the "Western" one saw three popes ruling simultaneously.

question.leadin: This pope probably died of injuries associated with a painful fall from his mule at Narni.
question.text: This 14th century Pope once complained that he couldn't hear enough screaming when some rebellious cardinals were being tortured. He was opposed by Antipope Clement VII during the Western Schism.

swap.leadin: An attempt to end this period at the conciliabolo, or "secret meeting," ended up creating a third faction by electing Alexander V.
swap.text: Name this period in which two, then three, people simultaneously laid claim to the papacy. The 1409 Council of Pisa failed to end this period.
swap.answerHtml: Western Schism [accept Schism of 1378; accept Papal Schism; accept Great Occidental Schism]
swap.clue: Pierre d'Ailly ("dah-YEE") and Jean Gerson ("zhawn zhair-SON") promoted a conciliar resolution to this conflict, which began when 13 rebels staged an election in Fondi ("FOHN-dee") with regalia stolen by a camerlengo.

question.leadin: Answer the following about syncretic misadventures in Asia.
question.text: This term refers to a controversy in the 17th and 18th centuries, mostly between Jesuits and Dominicans, over whether ancestor worship should be allowed in a certain country's practice of Christianity. A bull issued by Pope Clement XI in 1715
question.answerHtml: the <u>Chinese Rites</u> controversy [don’t accept other answers, this is a fairly discrete term]

swap.leadin: This event was preceded by growing tensions between Spoletan and Roman factions over whether Arnulf or Lambert should be Holy Roman emperor.
swap.text: Name this event in which Pope Stephen VI put the rotting corpse of his predecessor, Formosus, on trial, declared Formosus's actions void, and ordered the body thrown in the Tiber.
swap.clue: Give the colloquial term for the 897 trial of Pope Formosus, in which the pontiff was charged with violating canon law by his successor and by a pissed-off Lambert II, who had previously been promised the crown.

question.leadin: Jonathan Magin would surely want you to answer some questions about the First Crusade.
question.text: The whole shebang began when Pope Urban II made his infamous "God wills it!" speech at this 1095 meeting in France, inspiring folks like Adhemar of Le Puy to zip off to the Holy Land.
question.clue: Due to an adulterous relationship with Bertrade de Montfort, Countess of Anjou, Philip I was excommunicated at this church council, which was preceded by the council of Placentia.

swap.leadin: Michaelist sources, such as The Chronicle of Nicholas the Minorite, were cited as proof of the intransigency of this Pope during the Apostolic Poverty Controversy. FTPE.
swap.text: Name this Pope during the Avignon Papacy who succeeded Clement V in 1316. He quarreled with Emperor Louis IV of Bavaria, who under advice of William of Ockham, set up the antipope Nicholas V.
